title: Replacing Credential Sprawl with Organizational Memory
summary: A structured WordPress database replaced scattered credentials and memory-dependent access.
principles: Organizations should own their operational knowledge rather than depend on individual memory.
looking_back: Today I would add stronger field-level encryption, granular permissions, and access auditing. The central design decision still holds: critical knowledge must be structured, transferable, and retrievable.
body: Client logins, hosting information, and technical access details were scattered across email, notes, and individual memory.
The solution needed to fit the existing WordPress infrastructure, provide structured and searchable data, and treat the information as security-sensitive.
I built a custom WordPress solution backed by dedicated database tables for logins, hosting details, credentials, and related metadata.
Technical access information became centralized and retrievable by authorized team members instead of living in one person’s head.

perspectives.name: Julie
perspectives.text: The important shift was not from notes to a database. It was from personal knowledge to organizational knowledge.

perspectives.name: Harbor
perspectives.text: This removes a single point of continuity failure.

perspectives.name: Min
perspectives.text: ‘Someone knows’ is not a recovery plan.
